name: og_36_stochastic_protocell_ecology
description: Gate E ecology: does a cross-feeding protocell community out-produce the best single lineage at EQUAL feed, is the margin causally due to cross-feeding (knockout), and do low-count stochastic dynamics materially change it versus the deterministic mean-field? One StochasticProtocellEcologyProcess drives all arms: community (all seeded, cross-feeding on), monoculture (best single lineage, full feed, no partner), knockout (all seeded, cross-feeding off). deterministic=False is the exact Gillespie SSA (extinction breaks the ring); deterministic=True the matched mean-field. Option B (dependency-free SSA); GillesPy2/COBRApy = og-36a. Metabolism = sustained A1 community, NOT autocatalytic (A2 refuted).

n_lineages.description: Number of protocell lineages on the ring

n_seeded.description: Lineages alive at t0 (set 1 for a monoculture arm — the best single lineage)

knockout.description: Cross-feeding OFF (b_cross gated to 0) — the causal ablation

deterministic.description: Mean-field Euler ODE (True) vs exact Gillespie SSA (False)

feed_F.description: Shared limiting feed influx, held EQUAL across arms (NOT split by lineage count)

feed_Ks.description: Monod half-saturation on the shared feed S

cross_Kb.description: Monod half-saturation on the byproduct B

mu.description: Birth coefficient on the shared feed

k_byprod_wash.description: Byproduct washout rate (what a monoculture loses)

eff_spread.description: Heterogeneity of per-lineage feed efficiency (0 = identical)

mono_lineage.description: Monoculture arm: which lineage to seed (-1 = most efficient); lets the sims take the true best single lineage

seed.description: RNG seed (reproducible SSA trajectory / efficiency assignment)

ecology.doc:
Lightweight Gillespie-SSA cross-feeding protocell community (Option B).

A ring of ``n_lineages`` protocell lineages with integer cell counts. Each
seeded lineage grows (birth) on its share of a shared, limiting feed flux
(``feed_F``, Monod-divided by total demand) plus a cross-fed byproduct from its
upstream ring neighbour (saturating in the neighbour's biomass); it dies/washes
out at a density-dependent rate. The ``update`` advances the community by
``interval`` of simulated time via an exact Gillespie SSA (``deterministic=False``)
or a matched mean-field Euler step (``deterministic=True``), and emits the
cumulative productivity (total births), the total/mean population, and the number
of extinct lineages. Cumulative productivity at equal feed is the community-function
metric; extinctions are the low-count stochastic mechanism that breaks the ring.

_contract.summary: Stochastic (Gillespie SSA) cross-feeding protocell community vs a matched best-single-lineage control at equal shared feed: does the community out-produce AND out-persist the best single lineage, is the benefit causally due to cross-feeding, and do low-count stochastic dynamics materially change it versus the deterministic mean-field?
_contract.description: Chemically explicit, integer counts: one shared limiting feed pool S (influx feed_F, EQUAL across arms), K byproduct pools B_i, K cell counts n_i on a ring. A cell of lineage i grows on the shared feed S (Monod, emitting one B_i) or on its upstream neighbour's byproduct B_{i-1} (cross-feeding, Monod, consuming it). Feed and byproducts wash out; cells die. Shared-feed competition alone excludes down to the single best lineage; depletable byproduct pools give negative frequency dependence (a rare lineage's upstream byproduct accumulates and boosts it) that stabilizes coexistence and extracts extra biomass a monoculture loses to washout. community = all seeded, cross-feeding on; monoculture = the single most-efficient lineage on the full feed, no partner; knockout = all seeded, cross-feeding off (mu_cross gated to 0) -> exclusion reasserts. deterministic=False runs the exact Gillespie SSA (a lineage reaching 0 is extinct and breaks the ring); deterministic=True the mean-field Euler ODE on identical propensities. A dependency-free reproduction (Option B); GillesPy2/COBRApy = og-36a.

outputs.cumulative_productivity: total cell births (biomass produced) since t0 — the equal-feed community-function metric (dimensionless)
outputs.total_population: total live cells across all lineages (dimensionless)
outputs.mean_population: mean live cells per seeded lineage (dimensionless)
outputs.n_extinct: number of seeded lineages currently at zero cells — the stochastic ring-breaking mechanism (dimensionless)
outputs.n_alive: number of seeded lineages with >0 cells — community persistence (dimensionless)

math: feed growth i: n_i + S -> 2 n_i + B_i,  rate mu*eff_i*n_i*S/(S+Ks)
cross growth i: n_i + B_{i-1} -> 2 n_i,  rate mu_cross'*eff_i*n_i*B_{i-1}/(B_{i-1}+Kb) ; mu_cross'=0 if knockout
feed influx: 0 -> S at feed_F ; feed washout S -> 0 at k_S*S ; byproduct washout B_i -> 0 at k_B*B_i
SSA: next event ~ Exp(sum propensities); one reaction fires by inverse-CDF; integer counts; n_i=0 absorbing
mean-field: dx/dt = sum_r stoich_r * propensity_r, explicit Euler; productivity += (sum growth propensities)*dt

symbols.n_i: integer cell count of lineage i

assumptions: Lightweight dependency-free Gillespie SSA + matched mean-field ODE (Option B); honestly a reproduction, not a wrapped ALife/agent engine.
One shared LIMITING feed influx feed_F, held EQUAL across arms — so the feed-limited biomass ceiling is identical and splitting feed buys the community nothing by itself.
Coexistence is stabilized by DEPLETABLE byproduct pools (negative frequency dependence), not assumed; knockout switches off exactly the cross-feeding growth and exclusion reasserts.
A lineage at zero cells is extinct and cannot recover (no cell influx) — how low-count noise breaks the ring; the mean-field never truly reaches zero.
Per-lineage feed efficiencies eff_i are heterogeneous so 'best single lineage' is a real maximum; parameters are proposed_inputs, not fitted.

emitter.doc:
Generic Parquet emitter, hive-partitioned per ``partitioning_keys``.

The process-bigraph lifecycle drives the emit cadence:

  - configuration is written at ``__init__`` time from ``config["metadata"]``
    (only when ``metadata`` is non-None);
  - history rows arrive via ``update(state)`` per composite tick;
  - ``close(success=...)`` flushes the buffer and (when ``success=True``
    and a partitioning layout is configured) writes the success sentinel.

Durability-sensitive callers must call ``close()`` explicitly at end of
composite run; ``__del__`` calls it defensively but interpreter-shutdown
ordering is undefined.
